title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Can you name the glowing skull bone?
Look at the side of the skull.
Which bone is it?
It sits at the side of the head, around the ear.
Your jaw hinges on it, just in front of your ear.
It's D. The temporal bone.
Why it matters: it protects your inner ear, for hearing and balance.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Only one skull bone really moves. Can you name it?
It's the bone that's glowing.
Which bone is it?
The maxilla holds your upper teeth, and it doesn't move.
This bone holds the lower teeth and hinges to open your mouth.
It's B. The mandible.
Why it matters: it's the largest, strongest bone in your face.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: You can feel this bone right now. Name it.
Watch the small bone that's glowing.
Which bone is it?
It's not the maxilla, which holds your upper teeth.
This one forms the bump of your cheek.
It's C. The zygomatic bone, your cheekbone.
Why it matters: it shapes your face and guards your eye socket.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: The back of your skull has its own bone. Do you know it?
Watch the glowing bone at the back of the head.
Which bone is glowing?
The parietal bones sit on top. This one is lower.
It also has the big opening where the spinal cord passes through.
It's B. The occipital bone.
Why it matters: it protects the part of the brain that handles vision.

title: The Skull
question: Which bones are glowing?
lines: Two matching bones form the roof of your skull.
Look at the glowing pair across the top of the head.
Which bones are glowing?
The temporal bones sit lower, around the ears.
It's C. The parietal bones.
Why it matters: they protect the top of the brain and meet at the midline.

title: The Skull
question: How many bones form the nose bridge?
lines: The upper part of your nose is bone, not cartilage.
See the glowing bones at the bridge of the nose.
How many bones form the nose bridge?
Look closely: a pair, left and right, meeting in the middle.
It's B. Two nasal bones.
Why it matters: the lower nose is flexible cartilage, not bone.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: This bone sits right above your eyes.
Watch the glowing bone at the front of the skull.
Which bone is glowing?
The parietal bones sit behind it, on top of the head.
It's A. The frontal bone, which forms the forehead.
Why it matters: it protects the front of the brain and the eyes.
